investigations.question: When a replica that has already accepted its configuration's StopSign is re-synchronized by the leader (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync, e.g. after a re-established connection), does its reported accepted index stay within its actual log content, so that the StopSign keeps being observable as decided (decided index == accepted index) and the decided log keeps being readable?
investigations.hypothesis: No. create_log_sync passes the follower's accepted index (which already counts its stored StopSign as one index) as LogSync.sync_idx; sync_log sets accepted_idx = sync_idx + suffix.len() and then adds 1 again because the LogSync carries the StopSign, so the re-synchronized replica's accepted index becomes one larger than its log content while its decided index stays at the real StopSign position. The replica then reports the inflated index in Accepted, so a write quorum of inflated reports lets the leader set a decided index beyond the entries it can read.
investigations.discriminator: Nothing that a further source reading would change; only further executions. Both variants the earlier discriminator named are settled by source: a peer receiving a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot compacts to the requested index only when that index is within its own decided index (and then builds its own snapshot from its own range), otherwise try_snapshot refuses it with UndecidedIndex and handle_compaction discards the error, so the peer keeps its state rather than mirroring the leader's loss (knowledge 69d9dfec8808400f931ca863a93167c3-knowledge-0, material mod.rs 217-227); and the trim path cannot raise a compacted index above a live replica's reported accepted index at all, because its bound is the minimum over a per-node initialised vector. investigations.question: Does the drifted accepted index reach the trim decision? The leader derives its trim index from the minimum of the accepted indexes it has recorded for the configuration's nodes, and those recorded values are exactly the ones the re-synchronization inflates; the documented contract instead requires that all nodes have decided the trim index. Does a drifted minimum let trim remove entries that a replica has not decided, or push the compacted index past the entries a replica still holds?
investigations.hypothesis: Once every node's recorded accepted index is inflated above its content, the minimum the leader uses exceeds the cluster's true minimum content index, so trim can accept a trim index that some replica has not decided (against the documented requirement) and can push the compacted index past that replica's entries; a later re-synchronization of such a replica would then ask the storage for a suffix starting below the compacted index, which the in-memory storage computes by subtracting the compacted index and would underflow.
investigations.discriminator: Answered for every route this question named, so only a different implementation or build profile would move it: the in-cluster re-synchronization below a compacted index is executed and silent, the truthful-peer route is closed by the per-node initialisation of the recorded accepted vector, and the storage-level reads below a trimmed index are executed and abort under overflow checks (with the wrapping alternative argued from the same unguarded subtraction, not built). A build without overflow checks, or another implementation of the Storage trait, is the remaining way to change this answer; the question itself needs no further probe in this configuration.

The follower builds its Promise's LogSync from the leader's numbers - create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx) when its accepted round is greater, and create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx) when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater - and create_log_sync reads a suffix from the follower's own storage at that prefix.
investigations.hypothesis: For an entry type whose Snapshot is NoSnapshot, such a Promise aborts the follower inside handle_prepare, because create_log_sync's non-snapshot branch calls get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) and the shipped in-memory storage subtracts its trimmed index from that value without a guard; for the snapshot-capable type the same call takes the snapshot branch (the follower's own decided index is above the prefix) and builds a Complete snapshot instead, so the two entry types differ exactly as they did in the storage-level probe.
investigations.discriminator: A four-step run, with the snapshot-capable entry type repeated as the control. (1) With node 3 leading, append and decide several entries while node 2 is blocked, so node 2 never sees the Decide messages and keeps a lower decided index. (2) Compact on node 1 or node 3 - trim(None) on the leader, or snapshot(Some(decided), false) - so that replica's compacted index lies above node 2's decided index while staying within its own. (3) Unblock node 2 and let it win the election with try_become_leader, so its Prepare carries its own lower decided and accepted index to both peers. (4) Sample every peer's compacted, accepted and decided index at that moment and whether its Promise was built and sent, with any panic reported as an event field through the harness's guard. The decisive observation is whether a peer whose compacted index exceeds the numbers in the Prepare has its Promise built, and the control is the same four steps with a snapshot-capable entry type, where the Promise should instead take the Complete-snapshot branch and so should not abort.
